$bog_smalljs_landing_Feature1_text_text: An incrementally adoptable ecosystem that scales between a single component and a full-stack local-first app.
$bog_smalljs_landing_Feature2_text_text: Build UIs as trees of components. Reactivity is automatic, side-effects are explicit.
$bog_smalljs_landing_Feature3_text_text: Full rendering virtualization — components outside the viewport simply do not exist.
$bog_smalljs_landing_Hero_subtitle_note_: Dependency arrays, manual subscriptions, manual cache invalidation, effect cleanup — none of it exists here. Not made easier, made unnecessary.
$bog_smalljs_landing_Hero_subtitle_text: Reactivity lives in the framework's foundation, not bolted on top.
$bog_smalljs_versus_case_error_not_loade: The runner page did not load, so this framework cannot take part in the comparison.
$bog_smalljs_versus_case_error_timeout: The runner did not answer within 15 seconds.
$bog_smalljs_versus_case_invalid_frame_o: This frame scrolled out of view while it was working, and a browser stops drawing frames it cannot see. Run it again and stay on this case until it finishes.
$bog_smalljs_versus_case_invalid_other: This run could not be measured honestly. Run it again.
$bog_smalljs_versus_case_invalid_tab_hid: The tab went to the background during the run, so the timings measured waiting rather than work. Run it again with this tab in front.
$bog_smalljs_versus_case_invalid_timers_: The run took noticeably longer than the scenario expects: the machine was busy and the timers were squeezed. Run it again when things are quieter.
$bog_smalljs_versus_case_run_hint_broken: One of the frames did not load, so the three cannot be compared on this machine right now.
$bog_smalljs_versus_case_run_hint_hidden: Runs start only while this tab is in front: a background tab throttles timers and stops painting frames, which would make the numbers meaningless.
$bog_smalljs_versus_case_run_hint_loadin: Waiting for all three frames to finish loading.

$bog_smalljs_versus_intro_text: Pick two frameworks and see where they differ. Every number carries the source it came from and the date it was measured, and the crash tests run live in your own browser.

$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_method_body: Every value here comes from a measurement or from an outside source, and carries the link and the date it was taken with it. A metric counts towards a category only when both frameworks report it: otherwise the one with the fuller table would win on how complete its data is rather than on what the numbers say. Where nobody has measured yet, the row says so instead of guessing.
$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_note_builtin: Whether the framework ships it, or you reach for a library.
$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_note_code: How much there is to read, and how much of it belongs to somebody else.
$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_note_cost: What the dependency tree and the release history ask for over the years.
$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_note_edge: Four everyday situations running side by side in your browser. Press Run on a case and read what happens; nothing here is recorded in advance.
$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_note_market: How easy it is to hire for it, to search for it, and to find a ready-made part.
$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_note_speed: How long changes take to reach the screen, and how much memory is held while they do.
$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_note_weight: What the browser downloads, and how long it waits before the page reacts.
$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_score_empty: No metric both of them report yet
$bog_smalljs_versus_pair_suggest_body: Missing one? Name it and open an issue. Adding a framework means a data file with its measurements, and, for the live tests, a runner page — both live in the repository next to the ones already here.
